statement.excerpt: It has a right to about 49% of a for-profit subsidiary of OpenAI’s profits, up until a very complex point that may require litigation to resolve, but the for-profit hasn’t made any profits, and the for-profit is owned by a non-profit.

our_interpretation: This is a compound claim about profit entitlement, limits on returns, corporate structure, and historical profitability.
About 49% describes a contractual distribution share, not a revenue share or conventional equity percentage.
Owned by a nonprofit is read as having a nonprofit corporate parent; the wording does not necessarily assert sole economic ownership.
Hasn’t made any profits describes the subsidiary’s history since its creation through publication. An annual loss alone cannot establish that entire history.
The plain reading of profits is realized bottom-line profit. The post supplies neither an accounting basis nor an identified financial source, so accounting_basis remains unknown.
May require litigation is a possibility, not a separate firm forecast.
The metric_scope records the profitability component. Contractual distribution percentages require separate evidence and are not interchangeable with net income.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish an approximately 49% capped profit entitlement, nonprofit parentage, and no realized profits over the subsidiary's history on an identified, consistent accounting basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish materially different contractual rights or corporate parentage, or demonstrate realized profits during the claimed history. A difference between profit-distribution rights and accounting profit must not be treated as a contradiction.
